Maple Cream Cheese Frosting

Jump to Recipe

If you love anything with that warm, cozy maple flavor, you're going to want to keep this delicious maple cream cheese frosting recipe handy. It's rich, creamy, and smooth, with just the right amount of maple flavor without being overpowering.

This frosting comes together with just a handful of ingredients and takes only a few minutes to make. The combination of tangy cream cheese, buttery richness, sweet powdered sugar, and maple extract makes it perfect for cakes, cupcakes, cookies, cinnamon rolls, and so much more.

Why You’ll Love This Recipe

  • Quick and easy: This frosting takes just a few minutes to whip together.
  • Rich and creamy: Softened cream cheese and butter create an incredibly smooth texture.
  • Perfect maple flavor: Maple extract gives the frosting a warm maple flavor that pairs beautifully with so many baked goods.
  • Not overly complicated: You only need five simple ingredients.
  • Super versatile: Use it on cakes, cupcakes, cookies, cinnamon rolls, muffins, or brownies.
  • Easy to make ahead: You can prepare the frosting ahead of time and keep it refrigerated until you’re ready to use it.
  • Great for fall baking: Maple is such a natural match for cinnamon, apples, pumpkin, pecans, and other cozy flavors.

Key Ingredients

  • Cream Cheese: Gives the frosting a rich, creamy texture and a slight tang that keeps the sweetness in check.
  • Butter: Makes the frosting extra smooth and rich while adding plenty of buttery flavor.
  • Powdered Sugar: Provides the sweetness and creates that soft, smooth texture that spreads easily over cakes and desserts.
  • Maple Extract: The star flavor here! It adds a warm, sweet maple taste that makes the frosting especially cozy and super delicious.

Variations

  • Add cinnamon: Mix in a little cinnamon for an extra cozy fall flavor.
  • Use it on pumpkin desserts: Maple and pumpkin are a fantastic combination. Try it on your favorite pumpkin cake, cupcakes, or this cinnamon swirl pumpkin loaf.
  • Use it on your favorite fall desserts: It’s great on gingerbread cupcakes or soft molasses cookies.
  • Add chopped pecans: Sprinkle finely chopped pecans over the frosted dessert for a little crunch.
  • Make it extra maple-y: Add a touch more maple extract if you want a stronger maple flavor.
  • Add vanilla: A small amount of vanilla extract can add another layer of flavor.
  • Make it less sweet: Start with a little less powdered sugar and add more as needed until you reach your preferred sweetness.
  • Try it on cinnamon rolls: Swap your usual cream cheese icing for this maple version. It's especially good on warm cinnamon rolls.

How to Make Maple Cream Cheese Frosting

Step 1: Beat the cream cheese and butter until light and fluffy. Then, gradually beat in the powdered sugar.

Step 2: Add the salt and maple extract and beat until smooth and creamy. That’s it!

Expert Tips

  • Use softened ingredients: Cold cream cheese and butter can leave you with a lumpy frosting. Let both soften before mixing.
  • Add the powdered sugar gradually: This makes the frosting easier to mix and helps keep the texture smooth.
  • Don’t overdo the maple extract: Two teaspoons gives this frosting plenty of maple flavor. If you want more, add it gradually and taste as you go.
  • Beat until fluffy: Giving the cream cheese and butter enough time to become light and fluffy helps create a much better frosting texture.
  • Adjust the consistency: If your frosting seems too thick, let it sit at room temperature for a few minutes and beat again. If it’s too soft, a little more powdered sugar can help.
  • Let your dessert cool completely: If you’re frosting a cake, cupcakes, or other baked goods, make sure they’re completely cool first. Otherwise, the frosting can melt.
  • Keep it chilled when needed: Because this frosting contains cream cheese, refrigerate it when you’re not using it.

Maple Cream Cheese Frosting FAQs

Can I make maple cream cheese frosting ahead of time?

Yes! You can make the frosting ahead of time and store it covered in the refrigerator. Let it soften slightly before using, and give it a quick mix if needed to bring the texture back to a smooth, spreadable consistency.

Does maple cream cheese frosting need to be refrigerated?

Yes. Since it contains cream cheese, leftover frosting should be refrigerated.

Why is my cream cheese frosting lumpy?

The most common reason is that the cream cheese or butter wasn’t softened enough before mixing. Make sure both are at room temperature and beat them together thoroughly before adding the powdered sugar.

Can I pipe this frosting?

Yes! This frosting is creamy and works well for spreading and piping onto cakes and cupcakes. If you want a firmer consistency for piping, you can add a little more powdered sugar as needed.

What can I use maple cream cheese frosting on?

There are so many options! Try it on carrot cake, pumpkin cake, spice cake, apple cake, cupcakes, cinnamon rolls, muffins, cookies, brownies, or even banana bread.

What cake flavors pair best with maple cream cheese frosting?

Maple cream cheese frosting pairs especially well with pumpkin, carrot, apple, spice, banana, chocolate, and vanilla cakes. It is also a natural match for desserts containing cinnamon, pecans, brown sugar, or warm baking spices.

Why is my maple cream cheese frosting too runny?

Softened cream cheese can become loose if it gets too warm or is beaten excessively. Refrigerating the frosting for a short period can help firm it up, while additional powdered sugar can provide more structure if necessary.

How do you get smooth cream cheese frosting?

For the smoothest texture, use properly softened cream cheese and butter and beat them together thoroughly before adding the powdered sugar. Sifting the powdered sugar can also help eliminate stubborn lumps, particularly when the frosting will be piped.

Can you freeze maple cream cheese frosting?

Yes. Store it in an airtight, freezer-safe container and allow it to thaw in the refrigerator. Once thawed, let it soften slightly and beat it again to restore a smooth consistency before spreading or piping.

Maple Cream Cheese Frosting

Terri Weir
My maple cream cheese frosting is rich, creamy, and smooth, with just the right amount of maple flavor without being overpowering. This recipe will frost 48 cupcakes, a 3-layer cake, and all sorts of other fall desserts.
No ratings yet
Print Recipe Pin Recipe
Prep Time 15 minutes mins
Cook Time 0 minutes mins
Total Time 15 minutes mins
Course Dessert
Cuisine American
Servings 48 This will frost cupcakes
Calories 113 kcal

Ingredients
  

  • (2) 8 ounces cream cheese, softened
  • 1 cup butter, softened
  • 6 cups powdered sugar
  • ½ teaspoon salt
  • 4 teaspoons maple extract
Prevent your screen from going dark

Instructions
 

  • In a large mixing bowl, beat together the cream cheese and butter until light and fluffy.
  • Gradually add powdered sugar and beat until combined.
  • Add salt and maple extract.
  • Beat until fully combined and smooth.

Notes

  • Use softened ingredients: Cold cream cheese and butter can leave you with a lumpy frosting. Let both soften before mixing.
  • Add the powdered sugar gradually: This makes the frosting easier to mix and helps keep the texture smooth.
  • Don’t overdo the maple extract: Two teaspoons gives this frosting plenty of maple flavor. If you want more, add it gradually and taste as you go.
  • Beat until fluffy: Giving the cream cheese and butter enough time to become light and fluffy helps create a much better frosting texture.
  • Adjust the consistency: If your frosting seems too thick, let it sit at room temperature for a few minutes and beat again. If it’s too soft, a little more powdered sugar can help.
  • Let your dessert cool completely: If you’re frosting a cake, cupcakes, or other baked goods, make sure they’re completely cool first. Otherwise, the frosting can melt.
  • Keep it chilled when needed: Because this frosting contains cream cheese, refrigerate it when you’re not using it.
  • This is a doubled recipe: Because this frosting is so delicious, you’ll want to make a double batch. Cut the ingredients in half, if desired for a single batch.
